polityNote: Federal People's / Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. The first level of Yugoslavia was its six republics (and from 1945/1946 the autonomous province and region within Serbia); this file draws only the Bosnian republic, which the map lacked before OpenHistoricalMap's SR BiH row (1963-04-07 on; the build yields to it there). Drawn from 1948 because Sutorina left the republic for Montenegro in 1947 (day not stated), after which its outline is the present state outline = the union of the three geoBoundaries BIH ADM1 atoms (Federation, Republika Srpska, Brčko). Not drawn here: SR Slovenia (the Slovenian–Croatian republican line in Istria and along the Mura/Dragonja has double cadastral records and the 1954–1956 attachment of Zone B is not dated to the day) and SR Macedonia (the 2001 border agreement with FR Yugoslavia moved about 2,500 ha, so the pre-2001 line runs inside today's outline).

sources.title: Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina (Wikipedia, oldid 1377913723)
sources.says: People's Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina 1946–1963, one of the six republics; its borders, almost identical to the Austro-Hungarian condominium, were delineated with the People's Republic and inherited by the independent state.

sources.title: Sutorina (Wikipedia, oldid 1374942414)
sources.says: Sutorina belonged to Bosnia and Herzegovina until 1947, when it became part of Montenegro; a 2015 agreement confirmed Montenegrin sovereignty — so from 1948 the republic is today's Bosnia and Herzegovina.

spans.dateNote: Renamed Socialist Republic by the 1963 constitution (7 April 1963).
